summary: A 16-bit I2C analog-to-digital converter with four inputs, a programmable gain stage and selectable data rates. You pick the input pair, range and speed in the Config register, then read the result.

facts.text: The first byte after the address selects which register the next read or write uses.
Register bytes go out most significant byte first.

cite.q: Register bytes are sent with the most significant byte first

facts.text: Config bits 11:9 pick the full-scale range, six real ranges; codes 5 to 7 all mean +-0.256 V. Default is +-2.048 V.
The size of one count follows the range: 187.5 uV at +-6.144 V down to 7.8125 uV at +-0.256 V.
Config bits 14:12 choose the input pair: four differential and four single-ended (against GND).
Config bits 7:5 choose the data rate from 8 to 860 samples per second; default 128.
Output codes: +full scale clips at 0x7FFF, zero is 0x0000, -full scale and below clip at 0x8000.
In single-shot mode (MODE=1) writing OS=1 starts one conversion; OS reads 0 while it runs and 1 when done.

all: 1b : Start a single conversion (when in power-down state)
0b : Device is currently performing a conversion.

facts.text: Writing 0 to the MODE bit switches to continuous conversion.

cite.q: To switch to continuous-conversion mode, write a 0b to the MODE bit

facts.text: One conversion takes 1 / data-rate seconds (derived, not stated).

cite.q: Use the DR[2:0] bits in the Config register to select output data rates

notModeled: The comparator, the ALERT/RDY pin and the Lo_thresh/Hi_thresh behavior (the registers store values only)
The OS bit in continuous mode (reads as 1 here)
Offset, gain error, noise and input-impedance loading
ADS1113 and ADS1114 (this is the ADS1115 only)
